current_activity: becoming operational at Saint-Sauveur-Lendelin under Bradley, controlling First and Third Armies
notes: Event date: Breakout-18 p343 (12th Army Group operational at noon, 1 August; First Army under Hodges, Third Army operational under Patton). Event definition: the army group becomes operational. Relationship: SHAEF is the organisational parent (assigned). Montgomery's 21st Army Group coordinated both army groups in the field until Eisenhower assumed direct operational control on 1 September (CMH "Northern France" brochure; Pogue, Supreme Command ch. 15); some sources describe this as 21st Army Group operational control. Location: the headquarters opened at the Château des Mares, Saint-Sauveur-Lendelin (Warfare History Network; Wikimanche; dday-overlord); Bradley received Churchill there on 7 August and Eisenhower on 8 August. Avranches (the earlier point on this row) was the breakout area, not the headquarters, and is kept only as an area reference. Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for the château. The Army "Essential to Success" text cited in review could not be opened here (access denied); the location is confirmed by the other sources.

current_activity: SHAEF assumes direct control of the army group as Montgomery's coordination ends
notes: Event date: Breakout-32 p683: on 1 September SHAEF became operational on the Continent and Eisenhower took personal command of the ground forces, replacing Montgomery as pro tem commander. Event definition: 12th Army Group moves from 21st Army Group's coordination to direct SHAEF operational control; the higher-headquarters chain existed before (SHAEF authority exercised through Montgomery's coordination), so this is a change of channel, not the start of a relationship. Location: last-known position, not shown on the date. The CMH command-post list (World War II by Day) has the army group at Laval from 23 August and at Palaiseau from 3 September (C0489); a 12th Army Group history says Laval in August and Versailles in early September, and Eisenhower met Bradley, Hodges and Patton at Chartres on 2 September (a conference place, not the headquarters). So on 1 September the headquarters was at Laval or on the move to the Paris area; Laval is the last listed place, nine days earlier, with no stronger evidence for 1 September. Relationship: SHAEF operational control from 1 September; the 21st Army Group coordination (C0223) ended 31 August. Event support: high (Green Book, 1 September). Location support: low (last listed command post, nine days earlier).

current_activity: First and Ninth Armies pass to 21st Army Group; Bradley keeps the south of the Bulge
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p423: Eisenhower agreed on the evening of 19 December and the next morning ordered the division of command; p425: Bradley telephoned the First Army later that morning and Montgomery reached Hodges' command post an hour or so after noon). The hour of effect is not documented. Event definition: the Allied army group boundary is redrawn from Givet to St. Vith and the U.S. First and Ninth Armies come under Montgomery's 21st Army Group; the 12th Army Group keeps the forces south of the salient (in effect Third Army). Relationship: SHAEF operational control (direct channel since 1 September, C0489); the army group was not organic to SHAEF. Two outbound transitions follow from the one order, each recorded on its own row with its own dates: First Army to 21st Army Group operational control (C0520) and Ninth Army to 21st Army Group operational control (C0522); in the CMH tables both armies keep the 12th Army Group in the assigned column. The 12th Army Group's own relationship to SHAEF does not change on 20 December; this row records the army group's side of the change. Location: Bradley's headquarters was at Luxembourg City during these days (Ardennes p330, p423); city centroid, the building is not stated. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Luxembourg City. Event support: high (Green Book narrative; the same order is in the CMH tables as the 12th and British 21st columns). Location support: high for the city, moderate for the site (a narrative statement, not a command-post list).
